mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals tightening monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a >0.5% FEDFUNDS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances following a >0.5% UNRATE increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a weakening demand environment, which reduces corporate revenues and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances following a sustained RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a quarter signals supply chain disruptions or reduced manufacturing activity, which leads to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 45% of instances following a >2% INDPRO drop.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances following the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 300,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a tightening labor market and potential wage inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 300,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% signals a strengthening demand environment, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 45% of instances following a sustained HOUST increase.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth slows by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter and industrial production (INDPRO) drops by more than 1% in the same period, it signals a supply-side recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth slows > 1% QoQ and INDPRO drops > 1% QoQ
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances following the trigger conditions.
